extracted.intended_audience: mathematicians serving as reviewers for Mathematical Reviews / MathSciNet
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for composing and submitting reviews to Mathematical Reviews (MathSciNet) via the AMS interactive web form, including TeX formatting, bibliographic suggestions, and post‑submission edits. Targets reviewers preparing review text, classifications, and metadata for MR entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: AMS Web Sign In (recommended)
rubrics_metrics.description: Signing in is not required but provides the most satisfactory interaction; you need an AMS Web Account with your reviewer number in the Profile.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you sign in and have your reviewer number in your Profile, your reviewer information will be prefilled on the Interactive Web form (name, e-mail, postal address) and you'll get a list of all items presently out to you. After signing in, click 'Interactive Web form' then 'Submit Review' next to the item.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item identification when not signed in (MR Number)
rubrics_metrics.description: If you choose not to sign in, begin by entering the MR Number (seven digits) of the item to be reviewed and study the bibliographic data to ensure you have the correct item.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The MR Number appears in the upper left corner of the review sheet or on the first page of the item. After entering it, click Continue to reach the main data entry screen. If the item is not on your list, put a note in Remarks (e.g., if a colleague passed it to you).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer number (optional but helpful)
rubrics_metrics.description: The reviewer number is a six-digit number that appears below your name on the review sheet; entering it is not required but helps review processing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you have a reviewer number, enter it on the initial screen when not signed in so MR staff can process your submission more efficiently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required web form fields
rubrics_metrics.description: The interactive web form contains several fields; required ones are indicated with an asterisk (*).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fields listed include: TeX Type*, Reviewer Name*, Email*, Postal Mail, MSC Primary, MSC Secondary(s), Review Text*, Remarks. Fill required fields before submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: TeX type selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Select which TeX flavor you want used to process your review: TeX, AMS-TeX, LaTeX, or AMS-LaTeX (AMS-LaTeX recommended).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose the type you are comfortable with. If your review uses AMS fonts (e.g., blackboard bold, Euler), select AMS-TeX or AMS-LaTeX. Do not include \documentclass/\documentstyle, \begin{document}, or \end{document} in the Review Text box (they are inserted automatically). Scientific Word/Workplace users should choose AMS-LaTeX and use 'Edit-Copy As Internal Format' to paste.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid user-defined TeX macros and external packages
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not use your own TeX definitions (\def or \newcommand) or external packages; these will have to be removed during production.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid \input, \usepackage, \include and any nonstandard macro packages; their use prevents creation of a PDF preview or increases editing time. All user-defined macros will be removed during editing—this increases production time and expense.

rubrics_metrics.name: TeX special-character handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain characters have special meanings in TeX and must be escaped if used literally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use \# for '#', \& for '&'. The percent (%) character denotes a TeX comment—if you need a literal percent in text use \%. Commented-out material is not considered part of the review text during editing; optional material should instead be placed in the Remarks box with an explanation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review text entry or upload
rubrics_metrics.description: Review text may be typed directly into the Review Text box or uploaded from your computer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you use TeX on your local system, first process locally to ensure no errors, then paste the processed review (omitting preamble/postamble) or upload the TeX/LaTeX file using Browse and Upload. For Scientific Word/Workplace, copy as internal format and paste; uploading SW/SWP may not produce a PDF preview. If you upload the wrong file, you may browse and upload a new file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer name format
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer Name is a required field and should be submitted in the prescribed format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit reviewer name as: last name, first name, middle initial. If signed in, this is prefilled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Email address required
rubrics_metrics.description: An email address is required and used to send automated confirmation and for reviewer database updates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If signed in, your e-mail is already filled in. Automated confirmations are sent once per day, so allow up to 24 hours to receive them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Postal mailing address
rubrics_metrics.description: Postal mail address is not required on the form but keep it current for timeliness of future mailings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If signed in, your current postal address is prefilled. Provide updates via 'View My Reviewer Information' when your address changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematics Subject Classification (MSC) guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are asked to suggest 5-digit MSC classifications for the item being reviewed; primary and secondary classifications are accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommend a unique primary classification and optionally one or more secondary classifications. Enter classifications without internal spaces (e.g., '11D45', not '11 D 45'); separate multiple secondary classifications with a space. If you agree with suggested classifications, you may leave the boxes blank. A 'Browse the MSC' link is provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: References in review text
rubrics_metrics.description: If including references in your review, provide as much bibliographic detail as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include full author names, year, journal/book/video title, article/chapter title, volume and paging, and MR Number if possible. Correctly formatted references (including MR numbers) can often be found using MRef (a free AMS service). References you add complement any publisher-supplied reference lists in MathSciNet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remarks box usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the Remarks box to add comments about the review item that help editors or note errors in bibliographic information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use Remarks for comments about other reviews or for regular correspondence (use email to [email protected] for that). Use Remarks to indicate if an item was passed to you by a colleague, and to note your intentions if an amended review is submitted on a later day (e.g., that it should replace the original).

rubrics_metrics.name: TeX comments and commented material
rubrics_metrics.description: Anything commented out with % in TeX is assumed not part of the review text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you have optional material, put it in the Remarks box and explain. If a literal percent sign is needed in the review text, write \%.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submitting the review
rubrics_metrics.description: After entering required information, click the 'Submit' button to send your review to Mathematical Reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You will see a confirmation screen and the TeX processor will be applied to your review text. If the processor runs without errors, a link to view a PDF preview of your review will be provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensuring TeX processes correctly
rubrics_metrics.description: Take steps to reduce the chance of TeX processing errors and to get a proper PDF preview.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you have TeX locally, process your review on your system first to check for errors. Select AMS-TeX or AMS-LaTeX if you need AMS fonts (e.g., Euler, bold math). Avoid external macro packages and user-defined macros, which will prevent PDF preview or require removal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Making changes after submission
rubrics_metrics.description: You may edit your review after submission by using the 'Edit Review' button on the confirmation screen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may resubmit as many times as needed. If you amend the review on the same U.S. Eastern day, the new review overwrites the old one and only the amended version is processed. If you submit an amendment on a later day, place a note in the Remarks box indicating that the amended review should replace the original.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference lists included by MathSciNet (publisher-supplied)
rubrics_metrics.description: Selected journals' reference lists are included with MathSciNet Full Item information and are processed independently of review text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These keyed reference lists supplement but do not replace references you may add in your review text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automated confirmation of receipt
rubrics_metrics.description: Receipt of your review is confirmed by an automated e-mail system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Automated confirmations are sent once per day; expect up to a 24-hour delay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Updating reviewer information
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers can view and request updates to their reviewer information (classes/interests, name, e-mail, postal address) via 'View My Reviewer Information'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the link to change classes and interests (which determine items editors send you). Changes do not take effect instantly; the request is sent to Mathematical Reviews for database updating.

rubrics_metrics.name: If the item is not on your assigned list
rubrics_metrics.description: If an item you received is not on your list of review items, indicate this in the Remarks box.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide context (for example, that the item was passed to you by a colleague who was originally assigned the review) so editors can track assignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: File upload mechanics
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the Browse button to locate a TeX/LaTeX file on your computer and Upload to populate the Review Text box.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After selecting Upload, the file's contents should appear in the Review Text box. If the wrong file was uploaded, browse and upload a new file. Note that using upload for Scientific Word/Workplace files may not produce a usable PDF preview—prefer copy/paste as internal format for SW/SWP.
